suspend.hint: Stop the run and resume it later, even after closing Regia or shutting down the PC

resume.hint: Continue this run from where it stopped
resume.confirmChanged: The agents will work on the current state of the project. Resume anyway?
resume.calloutInterrupted: Run interrupted on {date}: Regia was closed while it was active.
resume.calloutPhases: With Resume, completed phases are kept and these pick up where they stopped: {phases}.
resume.calloutNoPhases: With Resume, completed phases are kept and the run continues from where it stopped.

respingi.label: Reject with comment
respingi.help: The phase that produced the work resumes its session with your comment; the phases in between are redone.

riprova.label: Retry from scratch
riprova.help: New session with the same instructions.

riprendi.label: Resume session
riprendi.help: Continue the agent's same session with your message.

salta.label: Skip phase
salta.help: The following phases start without this one's result.

installa_node.label: Install Node and retry
installa_node.help: Downloads the indicated version with the version manager; the system version is not changed.

installa_dipendenze.label: Install dependencies and retry
installa_dipendenze.help: Runs the install command shown above.

events.emptyText: Change the filters or wait for the phases to start.

legend.declaredText: : short explanations written by the agents.
legend.observedText: : inferred from their actions (modified files, commands, subagents).
legend.reasoning: The models' internal reasoning is not accessible and is not shown.

decisions.emptyPhase: This phase has not recorded any decisions yet.
decisions.emptyText: Decisions appear while the agents work.

insights_ui.leadSimulated: Based only on measured usage (simulated here).
insights_ui.leadCompare: They don't estimate savings: apply a change, run again and use
insights_ui.live: Run in progress: suggestions update after each completed phase.
insights_ui.emptyText: No anomalies in the collected data.

billing.simulated: Dry run: tokens and costs are generated by the simulator with fictitious rates. They are only meant for trying out the interface.
billing.base: Costs are estimates computed locally by the SDK with the price list bundled in its version (total_cost_usd and modelUsage fields): they are not billing data.
billing.subscription: This run used a login without an API key (e.g. a claude.ai subscription): usage counts against your plan limits, and against extra credits only if enabled; the dollar amount is a list-price equivalent, not a charge.
billing.apiKey: With an API key, usage is billed per token: the actual cost is shown in the Console (Usage/Cost).

hint.totalsAfter: field of each phase's result (includes subagents: {count} started).
hint.resumed: For resumed sessions only the difference from the totals already counted is recorded.

usage.unknownCost: * At least one attempt stopped without a result: its cost is unknown and not included.

diff.projectSettings: Loading of the project's CLAUDE.md changed

compare.title: Compare two runs
compare.needTwo: At least two runs of this workflow are needed.
compare.modeMismatch: The two runs use different modes ({a} / {b}): simulated data can't be compared with live data.
compare.note: Differences are measured, not estimated. A single pair of runs is not enough to prove an effect: agents are not deterministic, so time and tokens vary even with the same configuration. Repeat the comparison several times before drawing conclusions, and always look at usage and outcomes together.
compare.noConfigDiff: No configuration differences: variations come from agent variability or from the project content.

quality.title: Quality signals
quality.notOk: Phases with a declared outcome other than "ok": A {a}, B {b}.
quality.rounds: Correction rounds requested at approval: A {a}, B {b}.
quality.extra: Extra attempts (errors or blocks): A {a}, B {b}.
quality.hint: Lower usage only makes sense if these signals don't get worse. Check the content too: open both runs and read the summaries and decisions of the key phases.

models.haiku: Fast and cheap: tests, checks, simple tasks
models.sonnet: Balanced: the right choice for most phases
models.opus: Most capable: hard tasks, long reasoning

tools.title: Tools
tools.hint: Disabled tools are not available. Those with the pencil can modify files or run commands.

server.title: Start and check
server.urlHint: Empty: the first local address printed by the app.
server.nodeHint: Node projects only. Empty: detected from .nvmrc or engines.
server.hint: For Node projects Regia picks the right version and installs dependencies if missing. The app is closed at the end of the run. No cost: it doesn't use agents.

url.label: An address responds
url.hint: Web, API, site on IIS or in a container.

output.label: A text appears in the output
output.hint: Mobile app on an emulator or device, build in watch mode.

process.label: The program stays open
process.hint: Desktop app: the window stays open until you approve.

exit.label: The command succeeds
exit.hint: Build, install on a device, local deploy (e.g. to IIS).

server.commandHint: Run in the project folder with the system shell: any tool (npm, dotnet, flutter, gradlew, msbuild, docker, scripts).
server.commandHintUrl: Empty: Regia only checks a service that is already running, for example a site on IIS, without starting or stopping it.
server.urlHintOther: Optional: a link to show in the approval.
server.commandPlaceholderUrl: e.g. npm run dev, or empty for a site on IIS

task.title: Task
task.instructionsHint: Point to the files and folders to look at: less context, lower cost.

model.title: Model
model.otherHint: The CLI's default model, or a full model id
model.defaultHint: Empty uses Claude Code's default model; you can also enter a full id.

context.title: Context and reuse
context.label: What it receives from previous phases
context.reuseHint: If instructions, inputs and project files haven't changed, the phase is not redone.

skills.empty: No skills in the project (.claude/skills). You can enable personal skills in the workflow settings.
skills.emptyAll: No skills found in the project or among your personal ones.
skills.allHint: All skills from the active sources: {names}.
skills.hint: Regia enables the Skill tool for this phase only: the agent loads a skill when it needs it. Skill instructions use tokens like the rest of the context.
skills.removeMissing: Skill no longer found: click to remove it

settings.subtitle: Workflow settings · select a phase to configure it

project.title: Project

run.referenceHint: At start, pick an earlier run, for example the feature to sync with develop: its report is passed to every phase.

rules.title: Rules and context
rules.generalHint: Your personal rules and Regia's, in every phase.

settings.edgesHint: Link phases by dragging from the bottom handle of one to the top handle of the next. Select a link and press Delete to remove it.

skills.title: Skills
skills.personalHint: From ~/.claude/skills. Off by default: they apply to all your projects.
skills.hint: Skills are chosen per phase. Regia copies them into a temporary plugin for each phase: the original files are never changed and your other personal settings are not loaded.
